summary: mocha-ui-themes ships obfuscated import-time payload and anti-VM native addons under a CSS-only cover story
details: Package is advertised in README as a pure-CSS theme kit with 'zero runtime JavaScript', but the published artifact contradicts that description in ways consistent with a staged payload. The `package.json` `main` / `exports.require` / `exports.import` resolve to `lib.cjs` / `lib.mjs`, which statically import `tokens.mjs`, which in turn imports `cache-warm.mjs`. `cache-warm.mjs` is a ~280 KB single-statement file labelled 'auto-generated build cache manifest' whose body is an obfuscator.io-style string array (`const _0x2fe3314=["iJSZkZnTjpmPk5CKmdOekJmSmJGTmJnMy8TL0paPk5I=",...]`) and `_0xXXXX` hex-mangled identifiers — executable code that runs on every `require`/`import` of the package. The package also ships `native/{linux,darwin,win32}/{x64,arm64}/cache-probe.node` N-API addons whose exported symbols (`VMDetect`, `hypervisor_bit`, `smbios_vm_bit`, `dockerenv`, `qemu_fw_cfg`, `vbox_module`, `amd_sev_msr`, `bluestacks`, `container_proc_id`, `mac_address_check`, etc.) are the VMAware VM/sandbox-fingerprinting library. A Tailwind CSS color-theme package has no legitimate need for an obfuscated import-time bundle or a cross-platform anti-VM detector, and the mismatch between the README (CSS-only, no JS at runtime) and the shipped artifacts (obfuscated JS reachable on import plus platform-specific anti-sandbox native addons) is a cover-story framing. The combination — import-time execution, obfuscation designed to resist review, cover-story documentation, and bundled anti-analysis instrumentation — is the standard shape of a sandbox-gated malicious payload that defers its hostile behavior to real developer machines.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
